title: Make sense of years and calendars
description: Start with century numbers, understand leap-year rules, then follow the calendar reform that changed Britain’s dates.
introduction: A date looks precise, but understanding it takes a little context. First learn how years are grouped. Next explore the rule that keeps a calendar close to the seasons. Finally see why a historical date needs its calendar as well as its numbers.
prerequisites: No previous history reading required. The century examples use positive CE years.
outcomes: Place a positive CE year in its century.
Distinguish a calendar date change from elapsed time.

lessons.objective: Place years in centuries and check the boundary years.
Understand why divisible by four is not the whole rule.
Explain Britain’s eleven omitted date labels without imagining missing time.

glossary.definition: A period of one hundred years; conventional CE centuries begin in years ending in 01.
A calendar year with an extra day, governed here by Gregorian rules.
A change to the rules used to label and organise dates.
